evals.prompt: I just finished building a DSButton atom with variant (primary/secondary/ghost) and size (sm/md/lg) enums, plus an onPressed callback. Create the Widgetbook use case for it as a DS component.
evals.expected_output: Creates a Playground use case using context.knobs.list for variant and size enums (with labelBuilder), a boolean knob to toggle onPressed, and setCodePreview. Scope is DS_COMPONENTS. Uses developer.log instead of print. Does not add knobs for theme or color tokens.

assertions.text: Response uses context.knobs.list() for enum knobs (variant and size) with labelBuilder
Response uses boolean knob + ternary for the VoidCallback (enabled ? () => developer.log(...) : null)
Response does NOT add knobs for theme or color tokens

evals.prompt: I'm building a Widgetbook story for a ProductDetailScreen (app screen, not a DS component). What's different about the setup compared to a DS component story?
evals.expected_output: Uses APP_SCREENS scope. File goes in widgetbook_screens_path/features/[feature]/[screen]/. Required use cases: Default, Loading, Empty, Error. Uses wrappers/mocks, NOT real navigation. File is [screen]_use_case.dart.

assertions.text: Response uses APP_SCREENS scope (not DS_COMPONENTS) for app screen use cases
Response includes Default, Loading, Empty, and Error use cases for the screen
Response specifies using mocks/providers and NOT real navigation for app screens

evals.prompt: After creating my Widgetbook use case file, which commands do I need to run to make it appear in Widgetbook?
evals.expected_output: First run dart analyze on the widgetbook path. Then run dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs. Mentions NEVER use part '*.g.dart' in use_case files.

assertions.text: Response includes dart analyze before build_runner
Response includes dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
Response warns that part '*.g.dart' must NOT be used in *.use_case.dart files
